title: The diagonal divisor line in any projective-line model
statement:
theorem diagonalTrace_diagonalPic_factorization (Y : Scheme.{u})
    (f : diagonalSurface Y ⟶ ProjectiveLine Y)
    (hf : f = pullback.fst (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y) (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y) ∨
      f = pullback.snd (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y) (ProjectiveLine Y ↘ Y))
    (e : diagonalSurface Y ≅ ProjectiveLine (ProjectiveLine Y))
    (he : e.hom ≫ (ProjectiveLine (ProjectiveLine Y) ↘ ProjectiveLine Y) = f) :
    ∃ (L : (ProjectiveLine Y).Modules) (hL : Scheme.Modules.IsInvertible L),
      letI := hL
      diagonalPic Y =
        Scheme.Pic.ofIsInvertible ((Scheme.Modules.pullback f).obj L) *
          Scheme.Pic.mapHom e.hom (hyperplanePic (ProjectiveLine Y))

proof.text: Choose the Boolean canonical chart c of the projection f. The proved finiteP1_diagonal_picard identifies c*diagonalPic with H times q*H_Y. Its kernel-ideal invertibility is diagonalImmersion_cartier. This reuses the complete determinant calculation rather than repeating the four charts.

The comparison g=c followed by e is an automorphism of the standard projective line over ProjectiveLine Y, since c.hom followed by f is q and e.hom followed by q is f. Apply the generic hyperplane automorphism lemma to obtain g*H=q*B times H.

Set C=H_Y times B inverse and let L be the existing skeleton representative of C. It is invertible and has Picard class C. Pull the desired formula along c. Pullback functoriality changes f* into q* and e*H into g*H. Substitute the two formulas and cancel q*B with its inverse in the commutative Picard group. Pullback along c is injective because pullback along c inverse is its left inverse. This proves the original equality with no remaining diagonal-specific obligation.

proof_origin.place: Reuse the completed canonical diagonal Picard calculation, then isolate only the EGA II Remark 4.2.7 change-of-model step. The Picard transport and cancellation are proved directly in Lean.
